categoryRead: 22 Oct expanded mining sweep: strongest durable candidate category is profitable miners with reconciled FCF/commodity sensitivity (NEM/AEM/GFI), plus potentially lower-multiple aluminium cash flow (AA). SCCO profits exceptional but valuation rich and output down; the latest ICSG 14 Oct refined copper forecast has surplus 104kt 2026 / 368kt 2027, so concentrate constraints are not proof of all-stage physical deficit. Lynas rare-earth processing is already profitable but proposed Meteoric acquisition introduces dilution/capex. MP/UUUU remain policy/project capital-intensive; ALB Q2 turnaround is commodity-price sensitive. MSC (Malaysia) is underfollowed tin niche with only ~5.3% Q2 net margin. Strictly source-dated, research-only; consult latestExpandedSweep report and QA before capital.

developingTheme.mechanism: US tariff/inventory incentives are concentrating refined copper in US warehouses while reducing the free float available to LME/Asian markets. That raises near-term scarcity and backwardation risk even before structural grid/data-centre demand is considered.
confirmation: mine disruptions or slow refined-supply response
invalidation: demand weakens enough to loosen physical spreads

ideas.name: Freeport-McMoRan
ideas.thesis: FCX is the cleaner listed pure-play expression of a tightening copper market, with direct sensitivity to realized copper pricing but enough operating scale to avoid speculative-development risk.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Sep 4 around $72.8 keeps FCX close to the preferred $70-72 accumulation area; $66-68 remains the stronger support zone and >$80.25 is the major breakout reference. Stage rather than chase a squeeze.
ideas.catalysts: Persistent ex-US inventory draw, grid/data-centre copper demand, mine execution and any supply disruptions.
ideas.risks: Copper tariff/arbitrage unwind, China/global growth slowdown, Indonesia/operational execution, high spot-price mean reversion.
ideas.nextTest: LME/CME/Shanghai inventory geography and FCX production/cost guidance.

ideas.name: BHP Group ADR
ideas.thesis: BHP remains the preferred diversified resource platform because copper is its largest earnings engine while Jansen adds potash and Olympic Dam adds uranium by-product exposure.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Prefer pullbacks; diversified cash flows reduce dependence on today's copper squeeze but iron ore and large-project capex remain meaningful offsets.
ideas.catalysts: Sustained copper tightness, Escondida/Copper South Australia execution, Vicuña decisions, Jansen potash ramp and Olympic Dam expansion.
ideas.risks: Copper/iron-ore cyclicality, China growth, Jansen/Vicuña capital discipline and copper-price normalization.
ideas.nextTest: Copper segment cash conversion and project-return discipline rather than spot copper alone.

previousSnapshot.categoryRead: Copper is now the highest-priority metals development in Power Stack. The signal has progressed from a temporary LME squeeze into a broader inventory-geography problem: tariff-driven US stockpiling is pulling refined metal away from ex-US markets, LME copper is near record territory and Shanghai visible inventories are around their lowest since early 2024. Structural grid/electrification demand remains supportive, but the current price contains squeeze/arbitrage premium and should not be treated as a permanent earnings base. Gold remains structurally useful but was tactically demoted after strong US payrolls lifted yields and the dollar.
